measured.breakage: python3 conformance.py --engine dryrun --engine second --break-drift registers one operator arm ('branch') in the interpreted engine's dispatch and leaves the schema untouched. The run exits non-zero on the binding alone: the interpreted engine reports drift=["branch"] with schema_ops=6 and executor_ops=7, the compiled engine reports drift=[] - so the fault localises to one engine's wiring rather than to the vocabulary. Every contract-level assertion still passes: step_orders_identical=true, terminal outcomes identical, operators_exercised=6, and the only failing check on either engine is A2. Removing the arm returns the same suite to 39/39 on both engines

claimed: live mode until run on the host: GATEWAY_URL is unset here, so every operation in adapters/live.py below the reachability probe has never been executed against a running endpoint; the request shape, the cost figure and the correlation headers it inherits from the reference runner's gateway adapter are unverified

the compiled engine is this harness's own build, not a durable executor: it commits one state row per transition to its own log rather than to the state seam or to the durable-execution engine PASS.md A6 records as present and not listening, which is the default compose-operators-implement's open question states

the reconciliation leg of compose-operators' definition of done is measured only against the imported planner's fold, because no per-operator cost declaration exists in this repository yet (stage 4 of that skill's migration)

the standard row: no published standard governs the operator set, and the schema dialect it is written in is recorded unverified (F-b3-09). The declarative prior art the research records (X-end-to-end-066, X-end-to-end-067) was search-only and is cited as evidence that a portable definition is achievable, not as a standard adopted
tolerate_exceeded is admitted by the termination vocabulary and produced by no run here, because the example's parallel operator has no tolerate member - compose-operators' own open question
a crash mid-composition is not exercised: this harness parks and resumes at the gate boundary, and the kill -9 proof for a step belongs to harness/workflow
